organization: Centre for Public Legal Education Alberta (CPLEA)
rationale: CPLEA's mission is to help Albertans understand their legal rights and obligations, making one source-current plain-language traffic-ticket guide a direct topical fit.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the contact form described at https://navigator.cplea.ca/about-cplea/ and ask that a resource/editorial team member independently assess one reviewed guide.
risk_fit_notes: Fabsy is a for-profit service and CPLEA may prefer its own nonprofit resources. Disclose that status, request editorial review rather than endorsement, and do not contact CPLEA and LawNow simultaneously; they share a parent organization. Hold outreach until the linked page has recorded qualified human review.

organization: LawNow Magazine (published by CPLEA)
rationale: LawNow publishes credible, readable legal information for non-lawyers and has an editorial channel for courts and the Canadian legal system.
contact_or_resource_path: Pitch a topic to editor@cplea.ca; the current contributor terms are at https://navigator.cplea.ca/terms-of-use/.
risk_fit_notes: This is an editorial pitch, not a backlink request. LawNow's May 2026 terms require submitted articles to be original and not AI-created; do not turn these AI-assisted drafts into an article submission. Use a qualified human author, follow editorial terms, and let the editor decide whether any source or bio link belongs.

organization: Student Legal Assistance (Calgary)
rationale: Its traffic/bylaw practice expressly covers speeding and trial steps, so its caseworkers and clients overlap closely with Fabsy's educational audience.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the general office number on https://slacalgary.com/contact/ and ask to be routed to the Executive Director or student leadership responsible for education/resources; do not use the client appointment form for outreach.
risk_fit_notes: SLA already provides supervised pro-bono help and its material should take precedence for eligible clients. Ask whether the guide is a useful complementary resource; never imply a referral arrangement, seek client data, or ask SLA to recommend a paid service.

organization: Student Legal Services of Edmonton (SLS)
rationale: SLS publishes lawyer-supervised legal education, assists with regulatory/traffic matters, and currently marks its Traffic Offences pamphlet as being updated.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the Legal Education & Reform Project contact form listed at https://www.slsedmonton.com/contact; the homepage currently says services resume September 21, 2026, so recheck before contacting.
risk_fit_notes: Offer current-source notes or a complementary reviewed guide, not a replacement for SLS material. Do not copy its pamphlets or contact a client-service line for marketing. Its website warns that not every pamphlet has lawyer approval; independently verify anything Fabsy cites.

organization: BearPaw Media and Education (Native Counselling Services of Alberta)
rationale: BearPaw is an Indigenous-led Alberta public legal education publisher whose Adult Justice resources expressly include tickets and fines.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the general inquiry address bearpawlegal@ncsa.ca shown on the homepage and ask only whether the education team sees a useful, complementary role for a reviewed general Alberta guide.
risk_fit_notes: Do not imply Indigenous cultural authority, endorsement, or partnership. Lead by citing and elevating BearPaw's own resources where relevant; ask for guidance rather than a link, and accept no response as a no. A general commercial guide must not displace Indigenous-led information.

organization: Elizabeth Fry Society of Calgary
rationale: Its court volunteers support people with traffic and bylaw matters using legal-process information and resource referrals, creating a concrete resource-review use case.
contact_or_resource_path: Use https://elizabethfrycalgary.ca/contact-us/ and ask reception to route a non-client resource question to Court Programs or Legal Advocacy.
risk_fit_notes: The organization serves people facing financial and systemic barriers. Do not ask it to endorse or steer clients to a paid service; offer a reviewed guide for independent assessment and clearly identify free/pro-bono alternatives on Fabsy's page.

organization: John Howard Society of Alberta
rationale: The provincial office states that its primary focus includes public legal education, which may make a carefully scoped court-process explainer relevant.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the contact form on the cited page and select/request the public legal education or administration team, not a local front-line service.
risk_fit_notes: Its main focus is criminal justice rather than ordinary traffic tickets, so fit is narrower. Ask for an accuracy/resource assessment only; do not present Fabsy as a justice-sector partner or ask local service offices for commercial referrals.

organization: Calgary Legal Guidance (CLG)
rationale: CLG provides public legal information, justice navigation, and a curated Legal Resources page; its Community Court work also touches bylaw matters.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the general contact route at https://clg.ab.ca/index.php/contact-us/ and ask which staff member maintains public legal education or resource links.
risk_fit_notes: Traffic tickets are not a headline CLG service and its low-income clients may be better served by free help. Disclose Fabsy's paid/commercial status, avoid intake channels, and request independent inclusion only if the guide fills a verified gap.

organization: Community Legal Clinic (Central Alberta, Lloydminster, Medicine Hat and Fort McMurray)
rationale: The clinic provides public legal information and advice across several Alberta regions, and current third-party rights resources identify traffic/bylaw among its subject areas.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the general contact button/information on the homepage or info@communitylegalclinic.net and ask for the public legal education/resource owner, not client intake.
risk_fit_notes: The primary site does not foreground traffic in its current homepage copy, so confirm current scope before pitching. Never seek a paid-service referral from a low-income clinic; offer one reviewed province-wide guide for optional resource-page evaluation.

organization: Lethbridge Legal Guidance
rationale: It offers free public legal education in Southern Alberta and maintains a resource section, giving a regional audience for a province-wide traffic-process guide.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the general contact form at https://www.lethbridgelegalguidance.ca/contact-us and label the message as a resource/editorial question, not a request for client help.
risk_fit_notes: Its listed education topics do not currently foreground traffic law. Ask whether the topic is within scope before sending a link; do not request endorsement or imply that a commercial provider is part of the clinic.

organization: Edmonton Immigrant Services Association (EISA)
rationale: EISA provides newcomers with legal-system orientation, community referrals, and multilingual settlement support, so a plain-language ticket-process resource may answer a recurring practical question.
contact_or_resource_path: Use https://www.eisa-edmonton.org/contact-us/ and ask for the Community Settlement Services or Library Settlement Program resource lead.
risk_fit_notes: Fabsy's legal articles are currently English-only. Do not describe the guide as multilingual or reviewed in another language; distinguish the translated service overview from legal content. Ask settlement staff to assess accessibility and relevance without soliciting client referrals.

organization: Law Matters (Canadian Bar Association — Alberta Branch)
rationale: Law Matters accepts article ideas and reaches Alberta legal professionals, offering an earned editorial route for a neutral analysis of traffic-court evidence literacy or public legal information gaps.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the article-submission form on the cited page; pitch the topic and proposed human author's truthful credentials, not Fabsy's preferred link.
risk_fit_notes: Audience fit is professional rather than consumer. Submit only if a qualified human author can truthfully support the analysis and comply with editorial policy. No promotional article, outcome claims, disguised advertorial, or expectation that Fabsy will be linked.

organization: Alberta Court of Justice — Traffic Court
rationale: The court's page is the primary procedural source for the forum, ticket response, official Traffic Tickets Service, forms, and court locations.
contact_or_resource_path: Cite the exact relevant section and link users to the official service or form; recheck the page and the ticket-specific instructions before publication.
risk_fit_notes: Do not solicit a backlink, endorsement, or resource listing from the court. Never use court branding or wording that implies affiliation. The individual ticket and current court directions control.

organization: Government of Alberta — Fine payment and ticket response
rationale: This official page explains Traffic Tickets Digital Service, fine-payment consequences, current fine sources, and where to get ticket help.
contact_or_resource_path: Cite the relevant ticket-response or fine section and link to the official digital service when giving process instructions.
risk_fit_notes: Do not send commercial backlink outreach to the ministry or Court and Justice Services. Treat the page as authority, not as an endorsement; municipal and bylaw tickets may follow different instructions.

organization: Government of Alberta — Demerit driving suspension
rationale: This official page supports claims about conviction dates, demerit thresholds, suspension periods, reviews, and restricted-licence context.
contact_or_resource_path: Cite the exact subsection relevant to the driver type and cross-check the current Demerit Point Program and Service of Documents Regulation.
risk_fit_notes: Do not solicit a link. Avoid turning general thresholds into a prediction for an individual; ticket type, conviction status, licence class, record, and offence date matter.

organization: Government of Alberta — Alberta Crown Prosecution Service
rationale: The official page identifies the Advanced Projects and Traffic Office and describes prosecutor-review functions available through the Traffic Ticket Digital Service.
contact_or_resource_path: Cite only the specific institutional role or service function and link users to the official service rather than a marketing page.
risk_fit_notes: Do not ask prosecutors or the Crown for a backlink, quote, content review, or referral. Never imply that a prosecutor will negotiate, reduce, or withdraw a particular ticket.

organization: Alberta King's Printer
rationale: The King's Printer is the official publisher of Alberta laws and is the correct source class for current Acts, regulations, and citation conventions.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the Laws Online Catalogue and cite the exact Act/regulation, section, consolidation/effective date, and retrieval date; relevant direct PDFs include https://kings-printer.alberta.ca/documents/Acts/T06.pdf and https://kings-printer.alberta.ca/documents/Acts/P34.pdf.
risk_fit_notes: Do not solicit a marketing link. A disclaimer does not cure an incorrect statement of law; recheck effective dates and amendments before every substantive refresh.

organization: Canadian Legal Information Institute (CanLII)
rationale: CanLII is a credible nonprofit legal database for searchable Alberta legislation and cited court decisions, including the Traffic Safety Act and evidence authorities.
contact_or_resource_path: Use stable case/statute URLs, the neutral citation, and the currency note displayed on the exact page; prefer King's Printer for official Alberta legislation where practicable.
risk_fit_notes: Do not solicit a commercial backlink or suggest CanLII endorses Fabsy. Check currency on every use and read the full decision before paraphrasing a holding.

organization: Alberta Law Libraries — Motor Vehicle Law research guide
rationale: The public law-library guide curates Alberta motor-vehicle statutes, regulations, research tools, and legal-education resources, making it a strong research and outbound-citation source.
contact_or_resource_path: Use the guide to locate primary authority and direct readers to Ask a Law Librarian or public research services where appropriate.
risk_fit_notes: Treat as a research starting point; its page was last updated September 2025 and individual laws/resources may have changed. Do not ask a public law library to promote a commercial service or imply librarian validation.

organization: Law Society of Alberta — Find a Lawyer
rationale: The regulator's directory is the appropriate neutral referral for users who need to locate or verify an Alberta lawyer, including language and limited-scope filters.
contact_or_resource_path: Link users to the directory and accurately state that the Law Society does not recommend or endorse individual lawyers.
risk_fit_notes: Do not request listing changes, a backlink, approved-provider status, or endorsement for a for-profit traffic service. Do not scrape or repurpose directory data; the page restricts use to locating and contacting lawyers and verifying status.
